claim_source_complete_review.saved_paragraph: **KAG001.** Kaguya wants her art to have a place, its demands to be understood and its practitioners to be recognized. That desire is legible before anyone must defeat her. Watching Kisaki move, she imagines the opera club has not been abandoned and may perform openly again; explaining theatre to Cherino, she offers roles, masks, technique and training to an interested visitor. These are independently valuable ends: permission to work, pleasure in a craft and company able to attend to it. The later crisis does not supply their only justification. Her confidence becomes consequential when recognition is inferred from a ruler's movement rather than requested from its holder, and when school loyalty is demanded from others in the form she has chosen. # Kaguya: art, rightful criticism and the limits of demanded loyalty

**Reading boundary.** This is a complete proposed textual character argument for the existing source-scoped home. The name and represented life are substantial even though the present typed private-family index does not authenticate a Kaguya family. Public-source inward wording supplies particular fears and wants; it does not create BOND, MomoTalk, profile, performed voice or an intimate Teacher encounter. Source keys S01–S03 refer to the exact adequate analytical owners in §11. The already accepted Reijo–Kaguya relationship and required institutional/Kai responsibilities remain separate. Original source authorship is attributed; this author has received adequate accepted meanings, not replayed thirty-five original objects.
## 1. Core thesis

**KAG001.** Kaguya wants her art to have a place, its demands to be understood and its practitioners to be recognized. That desire is legible before anyone must defeat her. Watching Kisaki move, she imagines the opera club has not been abandoned and may perform openly again; explaining theatre to Cherino, she offers roles, masks, technique and training to an interested visitor. These are independently valuable ends: permission to work, pleasure in a craft and company able to attend to it. The later crisis does not supply their only justification. Her confidence becomes consequential when recognition is inferred from a ruler's movement rather than requested from its holder, and when school loyalty is demanded from others in the form she has chosen. [S01:81/85/87/125;3401:u0012–0015/u0024–0030/u0050–0065/u0083–0091; S02:100;839:004:u0075–0169]

**KAG002.** Her strongest contrary evidence prevents a simple picture of a false critic. The objection to Kai's shortcut expulsion and erased records has substance: Kisaki later admits procedure and fairness problems. Kaguya also refuses to become head, identifying a contradiction between defending tradition and violating it, and insisting that she and her members exist to perform theatre. The issue is therefore how real artistic and procedural commitments coexist with unequal remedies. Her categorical school-or-head demand, willingness to force a later expulsion and proposed public sacrifice cannot be cleared by the fact that part of her criticism is right. Each has recipients with different obligations and answers. [S02:124/128;839:010:u0006–0042/014:u0040–0106; S03:111/116/119–121;840:009:u0131–0164/010:u0058–0082/011:u0061–0090]

**KAG003.** The bounded longitudinal finding is a differentiation of choices, not a discovery that every apparent trait has one cause. She projects assurance, teaches and mobilizes; she collaborates unequally with Kai while naming a school loyalty distinct from that collaborator; she refuses the offered title yet accepts limited maintenance; she recognizes a need for greater caution while retaining remonstrance. Her newly felt appreciation of Kisaki's burden is a real change in represented understanding. It is not an apology, complete repentance or proof that her artistic convictions were abandoned. Her imagined return, actual renewed theatre, actual poor condition and ordered care must likewise remain separate outcomes. [S01:81/85/105–119; S02:120/128; S03:111/119–121/128]

**KAG004.** This character question concerns the conditions under which Kaguya's serious reasons become answers others are required to enact. It does not make coercion her permanent essence: an explanation of theatre to a willing guest differs from a forced political choice, and a title she refuses differs from a resource agreement others extract from her. Nor does it make her only a victim of authority. She can suffer restriction and bodily cost, identify a procedural problem, and still be responsible for imposed ends. The ordinary, political and bodily evidence belongs to the same bounded person without needing a private-source pool or a completed life history. [S01:69/81/85/113–125; S02:100/120–132; S03:111/116/119–128]
## 2. Longitudinal state and development

**KAG005.** The morning sequence starts with a report of activity restraint after an unnamed “例の事件.” Kaguya's observation of Kisaki becomes reassurance that her club has not been forsaken. Her members supply checking questions: they watched from a distance, and their unique dance needs explanation. Kaguya invokes reliable eyes and a supposedly all-knowing head, then recognizes that some movements need instruction. Confidence is thus not pure knowledge or empty fraud. She notices a real movement and gives it an interested explanation, while the people around her expose a gap between sight, purpose and permission. Neither a date for the unnamed incident nor a rescinded restriction follows. [S01:69/81/85;3401:u0024/u0024–0030/u0050–0065, actor seam at u0052]

**KAG006.** Mobilization turns that hopeful interpretation into an audience for Kisaki. In3403 she and Reijo make a shared movement bear different lifetime efforts, continue after Kisaki says it is neither specialty, and propose force when words fail. The children and Kokona then answer as frightened recipients, not useful symbols of another person's moral authority. Disputant apologies are printed, and exercise actually begins after intervention and further repair. The text does not print an enacted duel, enduring rivalry settlement or verified attendance increase. The local sequence establishes that passionate belonging can distort listening and that interruption can obtain an apology; it does not prove that every Kaguya exchange repeats this pattern. [S01:105–119;3403:u0006–0039/u0042/u0073–0113/u0117–0134]

**KAG007.** EVENT839 presents another context for her craft: an actual theatre exchange, a genuinely interested guest and an inward recognition that mixing schools changes both sides. Kai's appeal then locates her art and humiliation within an instrumental proposal. She initially refuses to explain herself and later articulates anxiety about commerce, outside influence and tradition. The political play, named remonstrance, coercive school-or-head demand and detention keep her position public and contested. EVENT840 explicitly follows that event at its own recap/continuation boundary; it gives her release by Genryumon, categorical title refusal, limited maintenance and a newly experiential question about Kisaki's burden. This local continuation can be analyzed without placing the separate morning into a universal before-or-after calendar. [S02:100/120–134; S03:79/109–121]

**KAG008.** The later remonstrator revises caution but not the fact of remonstrance. She asks for a public defeat that would restore Kisaki's authority; Kisaki refuses that path. The next account gives poor condition, treatment/transfer/nursing orders and postponed adjudication. Finally theatre and the festival have actually resumed. That positive return is not merely a future wish, but its scope stays local: the record does not supply individual recovery, a formal rescission of the morning's reported restriction, or a finished procedure for future dissent. A bounded arc therefore ends with continued artistic presence and changed recognition of burdens, rather than either unchanged rebellion or fully reconciled reform. [S03:119–130;840:011:u0061–0090/012/017]
## 3. Public and private self

**KAG009.** Kaguya's represented inward life makes her art more than a public emblem. The fear of abandonment and imagined assurance explain why Kisaki's movements matter to her, while the opera members' doubts preserve independent checking. These inward or private-style sentences are printed within GROUP evidence, not a separately admitted private encounter. Near-insults in3403 are also private-style wording at their exact units, not insults automatically heard by Reijo. Her internal commitment supplies reasons for conduct without giving other characters access to every reason or proving that the analyst knows an exhaustive personal interior. [S01:81/85/105/160;3401:u0024–0030/3403:u0032/u0037]

**KAG010.** Her public explanatory self can meet another person's curiosity. Cherino's interest in roles and technique, and disappointment that later performances prevent a walk together, make the encounter reciprocal without completing the wished-for walk. Kaguya's inward recognition that meeting changes both schools differs from Tomoe's suspicion of a concealed demand. It matters that the same event gives a willing audience and political resistance: her art is not intrinsically a trap, and visitors are not a single uniform reception. The adequate argument supports this particular contact; it does not authenticate permanent friendship, private travel together or universal approval of Shanhaijing theatre. [S02:98–100;839:004:u0001–0065/u0075–0169]

**KAG011.** Kai's first account of Kaguya's humiliation is an attribution directed at her. Her initial refusal to explain does not confirm it. Later anxiety and school loyalty are her own represented words and cannot simply be substituted for Kai's preferred motive. The alliance remains consequential—promised connections, challenged qualifications and an offered new drama give Kai leverage—but the source preserves a boundary around Kaguya's self-description. A responsible character account can take manipulation seriously while refusing to let the manipulator narrate all of her reasons. [S02:120;839:006:u0050–0148]

**KAG012.** Refused headship gives an especially strong test of public self against inferred ambition. Her refusal is actual and categorical, not merely Reijo's prediction that she is a stubborn artist. Yet refusing a title does not grant a private exemption from everything that follows: she accepts bounded maintenance and others convert reluctant agreement into resource authorization. The final inward question about Kisaki's burden is an experiential comparison, not confession of secretly wanting office or a completed moral correction. The self remains differentiated across art, duty, fatigue and disagreement. [S03:109/111;840:009:u0074–0090/u0131–0164]
## 4. School and club role

**KAG013.** Kaguya is expressly the 京劇部 director in the morning and theatre-club head in the exchange. That is a local role supported by the named argument; folder CLUB_024_001 does not place every actor in one club. She explains technique, leads members and imagines renewed public performance. The reported restraint after an unnamed incident constrains this work, but its precise legal basis and rescission are absent. Her authority over a craft is thus legible as represented work and recognition, not an audited certification or licence whose powers can be reconstructed from a title alone. [S01:34/67/69/81/85/87; S02:100]

**KAG014.** She gives loyalty different objects. The morning's supposed assurance rests on reverence toward Kisaki;839's opposition says school loyalty differs from obedience to its head. These statements need not be flattened into hypocrisy or a fully consistent constitutional doctrine. Circumstances and her perceived threat change what she asks loyalty to protect. Genryumon members hesitate at her school-or-head choice rather than unanimously accepting it, while Mina explicitly chooses protecting Kisaki. Their answers keep “the school” from becoming a single actor that Kaguya can speak for. [S01:81/85/113; S02:120/124–128]

**KAG015.** Her procedural objection is concrete: customary expulsion procedure and the deletion of Kai's records. She would reinstate, process and publicly expel Kai again, forcibly if necessary. This differs from believing Kai innocent or wanting Kai free to rule. It also carries the problem Mina articulates about safety and victims during the projected delay. Kisaki's later admission confirms a fairness problem; neither admission nor criticism supplies an inspected statute, lawful judgment or safe corrected process. The argument must preserve the critic's reason and the costs her proposed fidelity to procedure leaves with others. [S02:128;839:014:u0040–0106; S03:116;840:010:u0058–0082]

**KAG016.** The offered headship exposes a second procedural contradiction: she will not defend tradition by violating it, with Kisaki's whereabouts unknown and theatre remaining her members' reason for being. Her limited maintenance is a different commitment. Others invoke a debt to Kai, refuse to own the resource demand and turn her reluctant agreement into collective authorization. This shows how an institution can use a person's bounded assent beyond its comfortable purpose. Kaguya's new sense of the head's burden is meaningful, but no printed appointment or complete repaired authority follows. The required Genryumon institution synthesis owns the wider distribution of those powers; this monograph owns her actual choice and answerability within it. [S03:111;840:009:u0131–0164]
## 5. Ordinary life and intrinsic wanted ends

**KAG017.** The ordinary Kaguya wants a place where theatre can be practiced and shown. The morning's hoped-for assurance is precious because restriction and possible abandonment bear on actual work she values. Her interest in movement is interested attention, and her gathering of members is an attempt to make skill visible. Those ends deserve analysis even where the interpretation of Kisaki is mistaken. An account that preserves only the later threat would leave unexplained both the sincere value of her craft and what her mistake risks taking away from others. [S01:81/85/87/125;3401:u0012–0015/u0024–0030/u0050–0065/u0083–0091]

**KAG018.** The exchange supplies art as a meeting. Roles, masks, technique and training become something an outsider actually asks about; Cherino's desired walk offers a different form of company which performance commitments prevent. Kaguya's own inward recognition of reciprocal change gives the meeting a positive reach beyond prestige. There is no need to make the exchange valuable only because it later supplies political conflict. Nor should Cherino's wish be reassigned to Kaguya as an actual joint outing: wanted company and the work that interrupts it remain separate actors and outcomes. [S02:100;839:004:u0075–0169]

**KAG019.** Her artistic commitment is not identical to a desire for administrative power. The later title refusal says that she and her members exist to perform theatre. The actual resumed theatre in017 gives that statement a positive local endpoint, even while the crisis's secrecy and labor costs persist. It is possible to preserve the achieved return without certifying that the club obtained every hoped-for liberty or every performer recovered.
